input: Interview my uncle about his immigration story on video

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The immigration story could cover a brief overview or go deep into specific chapters — childhood, the journey, arrival, settling in — which determines how many questions to prepare and how long the interview runs.
Knowing who the final audience is (just family, a wider public, a school project) shapes the tone, language level, and how personal or sensitive the questions can be.
Whether the interview is in-person or remote, and what environment is available, directly affects camera setup, sound quality, and lighting choices.
The uncle's availability and how much time he is willing to give defines the interview length and how many topics can realistically be covered.
The recording equipment available (smartphone, DSLR, webcam) determines the technical preparation needed and the achievable video quality.
The desired tone — formal documentary style vs. warm conversational chat — changes how questions are written, whether a script is used, and how the interviewer should present themselves.
Knowing what the finished product should look like — a raw unedited recording vs. a polished edited video with titles — determines the post-production effort and tools needed.

gold.taskTitle: Interview Uncle About His Immigration Story on Video
gold.taskDescription: Conduct a recorded video interview with the user's uncle to capture his personal immigration story.

questions.title: Which parts of his story do you want to cover?
questions.description: Clarify whether the interview focuses on a specific phase (e.g., the decision to leave, the journey, arriving, building a new life) or aims to capture the full story from start to present.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for this video?
questions.description: Determine whether the video is for close family only, a broader community, a school or university project, or potential public sharing — this shapes tone and depth.

questions.title: Will the interview be in-person or remote?
questions.description: Establish whether you and your uncle will be in the same location or connecting over video call, as this changes setup requirements entirely.

questions.title: How much time is your uncle willing to give?
questions.description: Find out the available time window — 20 minutes, an hour, multiple sessions — to plan the right number of questions and pacing.

questions.title: What recording equipment do you have access to?
questions.description: Identify whether you will be using a smartphone, webcam, DSLR, or another device, so the technical preparation and quality expectations can be set accordingly.

questions.title: Should the feel be a formal documentary or a relaxed conversation?
questions.description: Understand the desired tone so interview questions, framing, and the interviewer's on-camera presence can be matched to that style.

questions.title: Should the final video be raw footage or edited with titles?
questions.description: Determine whether the deliverable is an uncut recording to preserve as-is, or a polished edited piece with intro titles, cuts, and possibly music.
